analysis:
Examined all supplied base/head source, patches and metadata against the indexed threat model and selected TB-002/TB-011 details. No concrete security regression is established in this scope. ProviderLoop+AppAttestShadow.swift:115,120 and ProviderLoop+AppAttestWorker.swift:10 permit update-retired worker recovery during holds excluded by refusingForServiceChange. Existing retirement success, generation, update-phase and shutdown fences remain; challenge custody still uses the parent's process key, and these changes do not themselves grant authorization (A-003, A-016, T-052/T-053/T-057). ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:11-16 separates add-on status reporting while still closing local and coordinator admission. Its new mailbox dispatch at :146 introduces an add-on control entry point, but the handler is not supplied, so validation or access-control absence cannot be inferred. Existing lifecycle shutdown still waits for accepted work, native ownership retirement and worker retirement. ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift:1189-1193 preserves the remembered serving set during add-on holds while retaining aggregate-capacity refresh; this is not evidence of substituted weights or cache/plaintext exposure (T-012/T-027/T-041).
Integration must examine the new drain owner and refusingForServiceChange definition, acceptPendingAddonControl's mailbox validation/access restrictions, hold release and lifecycle/update preemption, and temporary model unload/reload handling. Verify that releasing an add-on hold cannot reopen lifecycle-owned admission or discard an unreaped worker, and that retained model inventory does not advertise unloaded capacity. These missing PR-specific implementations leave material availability and authorization-lifecycle uncertainty; they are coverage limits, not findings. No supplied change directly modifies encryption, billing, privileged fan authority or attestation-policy verification.
